Hi Sergio / Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week — LumaCloud is excited to kick off the pilot. Before we get scheduled for technical onboarding, our procurement team asked for a quick checklist so they can issue a PO. A few specific asks: 

- Can you confirm what vendor setup docs you need (W-9 / COI / vendor questionnaire)?
- Typical turnaround: once vendor docs are submitted, how long until Redwood issues a PO?
- Preferred line-item format: do you expect separate line items for usage (token credits) vs. dedicated capacity vs. support? Any recommended SKU naming conventions?
- Any standard PO fields Redwood requires on the invoice (cost center, site code, PO contact)?

We have attached our vendor intake form to this thread. If you can send a short checklist and an example PO line-item sample, our procurement lead (procurement@lumacloud.com) will validate internally and push a PO.

Attachments: [Attachment: LumaCloud_Vendor_Intake_Form.pdf (application/pdf)]

Best,

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@lumacloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: vendor onboarding + PO cadence question

Alice — thanks for sending this over. Quick answers and a proposed cadence so procurement has something to action: 

1) Vendor docs we need:
   - Completed vendor intake form (you attached it — perfect)
   - W-9 (for US entities) or equivalent tax form for non-US
   - Vendor bank details and remittance address
   - Copy of authorized signatory (for contract signatures) — we accept DocuSign

2) Typical timing (standard case):
   - Vendor intake + W-9 received: Day 0
   - Internal vendor setup in finance: 1–2 business days
   - Review and SOW/quote finalization: 1–3 business days (depending on change requests)
   - PO issuance: typically within 2–5 business days after vendor setup and quote acceptance

   If procurement wants an expedited partial PO for pilot credits, we can do a pro-forma PO same day once the intake and W-9 are in our portal — we’ll mark it as pilot credits and keep the remainder pending SOW sign-off.

3) Line-item guidance (recommended):
   - Keep charge types distinct for clarity and invoicing:
     a) Managed inference usage (token credits) — quantity = number of credits, unit = credits, unit price = $/credit
     b) Dedicated capacity (monthly reservation) — quantity = months, unit = month, unit price = $/month
     c) One-time onboarding / integration fee — quantity = 1, unit = each
     d) Support retainer (if applicable) — quantity = months, unit = month

   - Suggested SKU convention: RW-<product>-<tier>-<unit> (e.g., RW-INFER-STD-CREDIT, RW-DEDI-XL-MO)
   - For multi-line budgets, include a short free-text description per line with account/cost-center code if available

4) Invoice / PO fields we require: vendor legal name, billing address, Redwood PO number (we’ll provide), Redwood remittance instructions (bank wire/ACH), and payment terms (default Net30). If finance needs Net45/Net60, please indicate early — we’ll route for approval.

I’ve attached a small CSV example with how we structure PO line items and column headers: Redwood_PO_LineItem_Example.csv. Dev — tagging you on technical nomenclature in case LumaCloud needs exact wording on usage credits vs. inference units.

Next steps: can procurement send final vendor data + W-9 to procurement@redwood.ai? Once we have that I’ll coordinate with finance and confirm an estimated PO issuance date. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Redwood_PO_LineItem_Example.csv (text/csv)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@lumacloud.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: vendor onboarding + PO cadence question

Looping in a few finance points from our side — these tend to speed things up if shared up front with procurement: 

- Payment terms: default Net30 on initial pilot. If LumaCloud needs Net45/Net60, we’ll need an approval from FP&A; please flag this on the PO so we can start that workflow.
- Cost center / GL code: include your internal cost center on each line item if you want charges mapped directly. If omitted, finance will allocate to the account default and we can re-code later via an invoice amendment (slower).
- Tax & EIN: please attach a W-9 (you mentioned) and confirm the legal entity name exactly as it should appear on the invoice.
- Attachments: I’m adding our internal line-item catalog — it lists canonical categories and short descriptions that our billing team expects. Using the categories in the catalog prevents back-and-forth reconciliations.

Small suggestion on the PO structure: group recurring services (dedicated capacity + support) as one line item per month and put variable usage as a separate consumable line with a clearly defined unit of measure. That makes month-to-month reconciliation straightforward.

If you want, we can provisionally generate a pro-forma PO for pilot credits within one business day of receiving the W-9 — indicate clearly in the email that the PO is limited to pilot credits and the remaining committed spend will be issued after SOW sign-off.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Finance Lead, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Finance_LineItem_Catalog.pdf (application/pdf)]
